title: Campus Council Approves Housing Expansion
content:
In a unanimous vote, the campus council approved funding for a new residential complex that will add 600 beds by 2026.

Administrators highlighted sustainable design elements and affordability guarantees for incoming students.
excerpt: Council gives green light to the largest housing project in a decade.

title: SGA Launches Tuition Transparency Dashboard
content:
Student Government released an online dashboard allowing students to track tuition spending categories.

The tool breaks down capital projects, faculty hiring, and financial aid distribution in real time.
excerpt: New dashboard demystifies tuition allocation for current students.

title: City Transit Adds Late-Night Shuttle for Campus
content:
Atlanta Transit Authority introduced a pilot shuttle that runs every 30 minutes between Tech Square and Midtown after midnight.

The partnership emerged after a series of student safety forums and will be evaluated at the end of the semester.
excerpt: New shuttle responds to student calls for safer late-night travel.

title: Research Labs Secure NSF Grant for AI Safety
content:
A consortium of campus labs won a $4.5 million NSF grant to investigate AI safety frameworks for autonomous systems.

The grant funds undergraduate research stipends and partnerships with local industry leaders.
excerpt: NSF award positions Tech researchers at the forefront of AI safety.

title: Tech Dining Overhauls Meal Plan Options
content:
Beginning in fall 2024, campus dining will offer three customizable plans with expanded halal, vegan, and allergen-friendly stations.

Administrators say pricing will stay flat while eliminating the 150-swipe requirement.
excerpt: Dining revamp promises more flexibility without cost increases.

title: Faculty Senate Backs Pass/Fail Expansion
content:
The Faculty Senate approved a pilot allowing juniors and seniors to take up to six credits of electives pass/fail without GPA penalties.

The policy goes to the Provost’s office for final approval later this month.
excerpt: Pass/fail flexibility could arrive for upperclass students by fall.

title: Campus Police Release Annual Safety Report
content:
GT Police Department published its annual Clery report noting a 9% decrease in on-campus theft but a rise in scooter-related accidents.

Officials plan new lighting audits and scooter safety workshops this spring.
excerpt: Latest safety report points to declining theft but emerging challenges.

title: Tech Hosts Regional STEM Policy Summit
content:
Policy makers from across the Southeast met on campus to design STEM workforce pathways, with breakout sessions led by Tech faculty and students.

The summit concluded with a resolution advocating for expanded undergraduate research funding.
excerpt: Regional summit highlights Tech's role in shaping STEM policy.

title: Wellness Ambassadors Launch Peer Support Pods
content:
Counseling Center wellness ambassadors introduced small peer support pods aimed at easing the transition for first-year students.

The pods meet weekly to focus on stress management, building community, and navigating campus resources.
excerpt: Peer-led support pods give first-years a new way to find community.

title: Campus Farmers Market Returns With Local Vendors
content: The weekly campus farmers market reopened for spring featuring 25 local vendors, cooking demos, and discounted produce bundles for students with SNAP benefits.
excerpt: Spring farmers market embraces local food and affordability.

title: Residence Life Hosts DIY Dorm Makeover Contest
content:
Residence Life rolled out a dorm makeover competition encouraging students to upcycle furniture and showcase creative storage solutions.

Winners receive gift cards to the campus bookstore and sustainability swag bags.
excerpt: DIY contest sparks creativity and sustainability in dorm spaces.

title: Student Chefs Share Budget-Friendly Meal Prep
content: The Culinary Club hosted a workshop on meal prepping with limited kitchen access, sharing recipes and ingredient swaps for dorm cooking.
excerpt: Culinary Club proves healthy meal prep is possible without a full kitchen.

title: Health Center Expands Teletherapy Hours
content: Campus Health announced extended teletherapy hours with evening and weekend appointments to better serve graduate and co-op students.
excerpt: Expanded teletherapy aims to meet growing demand for counseling support.

title: Outdoor Recreation Club Plans Spring Adventure Series
content: The Outdoor Recreation Club unveiled a spring series including hiking, paddle boarding, and overnight camping trips with beginner-friendly pricing.
excerpt: Adventure series invites students to explore Georgia's natural spaces.

title: Career Center Hosts Women in Tech Networking Night
content: More than 200 students attended a networking night connecting women in tech with alumnae mentors and recruiters from partner companies.
excerpt: Networking night bridges students with alumnae leaders in tech.

title: Artisans Collective Opens Pop-Up Studio on Campus
content: A student-run artisans collective opened a pop-up studio in the Student Center offering weekend workshops in ceramics, fiber arts, and screen printing.
excerpt: Pop-up studio gives creatives a collaborative space to learn new crafts.

title: Editorial: Tech Must Address Accessibility in New Builds
content: With new construction underway across campus, our editorial board urges administrators to prioritize universal design principles and student input on accessibility features.
excerpt: Editorial board presses for universal design in upcoming projects.

title: Column: Why Mentorship Matters for First-Gen Students
content: As a first-generation student, I found mentorship essential for navigating unwritten rules. Tech should invest in expanded mentorship programs pairing first-gen students with faculty allies.
excerpt: Opinion writer advocates for more robust mentorship for first-gen students.

title: Guest Column: Invest in Atlanta's Tech Corridor
content: City council member Jordan Ellis argues for transit investments linking Tech Square with growing tech hubs to support talent retention and equitable growth.
excerpt: City leader calls for transit-focused investments in the tech corridor.

title: Editorial: Protect Student Journalism Funding
content: The Technique editorial board urges campus leaders to safeguard student media funding amid ongoing budget realignments and advertising shortfalls.
excerpt: Editorial argues that student voices require stable institutional support.

title: Column: Redesigning Tech Walkway for Pedestrian Safety
content: With scooter and bike traffic increasing, Tech Walkway needs better lane separation, clearer signage, and enforcement to protect pedestrians.
excerpt: Opinion writer proposes concrete steps to keep Tech Walkway safe.

title: Editorial: Let Students Lead Sustainability Projects
content: Student organizations have piloted successful sustainability projects; administration should scale them with funding, mentorship, and institutional backing.
excerpt: Editorial calls for institutional support of student-led sustainability ideas.

title: Column: Redefining Success Beyond GPA
content: Tech culture often equates success with GPA. It's time to recognize learning, creativity, and community impact as equally meaningful achievements.
excerpt: Opinion urges students to broaden their definition of success.

title: Editorial: Celebrate the Hidden Labor on Campus
content: Custodial staff, dining workers, and maintenance teams keep Tech running. Administration should spotlight their contributions and improve compensation.
excerpt: Editorial argues for recognition and pay equity for essential staff.

title: Student Theatre Debuts Original Sci-Fi Production
content: The DramaTech troupe premiered an original sci-fi play written and directed by students, blending practical effects with projection mapping.
excerpt: DramaTech's new production pushes boundaries with sci-fi storytelling.

title: Indie Film Showcase Spotlights Student Directors
content: The Tech Film Society curated a slate of student-produced short films exploring themes of identity, climate anxiety, and campus humor.
excerpt: Film society celebrates student storytellers with indie showcase.

title: Campus Orchestra Prepares for Spring Gala
content: The Tech Symphony Orchestra is rehearsing a genre-spanning setlist featuring classical works, anime themes, and a surprise EDM mashup for the spring gala.
excerpt: Symphony orchestra mixes genres for an adventurous spring program.

title: Esports Arena Hosts Collegiate Valorant Invitational
content: Tech's esports arena welcomed teams from across the Southeast for a weekend-long Valorant invitational, complete with shoutcasters and live audience.
excerpt: Valorant invitational showcases Tech's growing esports scene.

title: Dance Team Captures Top Honors at Nationals
content: Tech's Goldrush dance team won the contemporary division at NDA Nationals with a performance inspired by Atlanta's civil rights history.
excerpt: Goldrush brings home national title with poignant choreography.

title: Local Band Premieres New EP at Student Center
content: Indie rock trio Midtown Mosaic debuted their latest EP during a packed show at the Student Center, featuring collaborations with Tech's music tech students.
excerpt: Midtown Mosaic's EP release draws a crowd to the Student Center stage.

title: Student Art Walk Celebrates Black Creatives
content: The Black Student Alumni Connection hosted an art walk featuring Black student painters, sculptors, and digital artists across campus galleries.
excerpt: Art walk shines a spotlight on Black creatives and their work.

title: Board Game Club Hosts Mega Marathon Weekend
content: The Board Game Club hosted a 48-hour marathon featuring indie tabletop designers, charity raffles, and a giant Settlers of Catan tournament.
excerpt: Board Game Club's marathon packs the student center with players.

title: Eagles Baseball Shuts Out Coastal in Season Opener
content: Behind a complete game from ace pitcher Tyler James, the Eagles blanked Coastal State 6-0 to open the season with a statement win.
excerpt: Tyler James tosses a shutout as Eagles baseball starts hot.

title: Softball Walks Off Rival Panthers in Extra Innings
content: Sophomore shortstop Maya Kirk delivered a walk-off double in the 10th inning to lift the Eagles over the Panthers in a thriller at Mewborn Field.
excerpt: Maya Kirk's walk-off double caps an instant softball classic.

title: Men's Basketball Upsets Ranked Rival on the Road
content: Led by senior guard Nina Chen's 28 points, the Eagles stunned No. 14 Metro University 78-74 with clutch defense down the stretch.
excerpt: Chen shines in statement road win over a ranked opponent.

title: Track and Field Sets Records at Indoor Invitational
content: Tech track athletes broke three program indoor records at the Clemson Invitational, highlighted by freshman sprinter Alexis Brown's 200m time.
excerpt: Track team shatters records and builds momentum for championships.

title: Women's Tennis Sweeps Opening Weekend Matches
content: The women's tennis squad swept their doubleheader against Mercer and Georgia State, anchored by dominant singles play from senior captain Isla Moreno.
excerpt: Women's tennis opens the season with two decisive sweeps.

title: Club Ultimate Qualifies for Nationals
content: Tech's club Ultimate Frisbee team punched their ticket to nationals after a dramatic universe-point victory over Georgia College in the regional final.
excerpt: Ultimate team earns nationals berth with thrilling universe-point win.

title: Rowing Team Opens Season with Regatta Sweep
content: In their first outing of the year, the rowing team swept gold across varsity eight, novice eight, and four events at the Lanier Winter Regatta.
excerpt: Rowing squad starts strong by sweeping the season-opening regatta.

title: Gymnastics Scores Season-High in Home Meet
content: The gymnastics team posted a season-high 196.450 to defeat Clemson and NC State, highlighted by sophomore Ava Patel's 9.925 on beam.
excerpt: Gymnastics hits its stride with a season-best team score at home.
